title: Constrained Code Generation with Diffusion Language Models
claim: Our constraint-aware method consistently beats baselines across functionality, syntax, and security benchmarks and model backbones.
layout: 3 grouped bar-chart sections, left-to-right, legend on top, ours in blue
description: A single wide grouped bar chart split into three shaded sections labeled Functionality, Syntax, and Security along the bottom. Within each section, clusters of bars are grouped by benchmark (HE-X, MBPP, CWEval, LLMSecEval+) and by backbone (DiffuCoder 7B, Dream-Coder 7B). abstract: Diffusion language models (DLMs) are a powerful, emerging paradigm for code generation. They construct programs through iterative refinement of partially corrupted token sequences and enable parallel token refinement. Importantly, this paradigm exposes a global program state at each denoising step, which provides a natural intervention point for enforcing program-level functionality and security constraints, guiding the generation before the final code is committed. Building on this observation, the paper introduces Constrained Diffusion for Code (CDC), an inference-time neurosymbolic framework that integrates constraint satisfaction directly into the reverse denoising process without retraining the base diffusion model. CDC augments the base diffusion sampler with constraint-aware denoising operators that combine mathematical optimization with program analysis to identify constraint-relevant regions of the intermediate program state and locally adjust the denoising trajectory, steering generation toward feasible programs while remaining close to the base model. Across code generation benchmarks, CDC consistently improves constraint satisfaction in functional correctness, security, and even syntax, outperforming diffusion and autoregressive baselines with less corrective computation and more localized edits.
